subtopic: Online communities, echo chambers and moderation
subtype: Banned or blocked from a group [Receiver]
passage:
Bidisha's diary, Tuesday night.
Banned from the film-club group today. Three thousand members, and one message from Sachin, the moderator: “Third spoiler warning ignored. You are removed.” I was so angry my hands shook. I had posted a spoiler as a joke, then argued with him in the thread while other people liked his replies. Nobody stood up for me. My first thought was that they're all petty. My second, a bit ashamed, was that the rule was fair and I did break it three times. And under all that, strangely, a small relief: I'll get my evenings back. Still, I used to check that group every morning. Tomorrow I'll go to the coffee shop and see if any of the real-life regulars are around.
Bidisha

qa.q: How many spoiler warnings had Bidisha ignored?
qa.a: Bidisha had ignored three spoiler warnings.

qa.q: What mix of feelings did Bidisha have about being banned?
qa.a: Bidisha felt rejected and angry, then a bit ashamed that the rule was fair, and also a small relief at getting evenings back.

qa.q: What could Bidisha do next to cope with losing this group?
qa.a: Bidisha could go to the coffee shop to see the real-life regulars, as planned, and find another way to talk about films without the daily check.

qa.q: How might Sachin have seen the ban?
qa.a: Sachin probably saw it as applying a written rule fairly after three warnings, though Sachin may also feel the strain of arguing in front of three thousand members.

grounding: A person removed from an online community feels rejected, angry and slightly relieved, since being cut off from belonging stings even when the rule was fair.
